questions.name: Returning client with a problem - allow more time
questions.text: Give time to clients who need it: returning clients with problems need the most. Understand the problem and help resolve it, whether that means managing side effects, treating a condition, or helping the client switch method.
questions.detail: WHO DAK decision support FP.DT.01

questions.name: Routine continuation - little counselling needed
questions.text: Many clients return with no problems and need little counselling. Provide more supplies or routine follow-up, ask whether the client has any questions, and confirm the method is still the one they want.
questions.detail: WHO DAK decision support FP.DT.01

questions.name: Issues and concerns
questions.detail: For returning/follow-up clients, if there are issues and concerns with contraception the client would like to discuss (e.g. Side-effects or symptoms with current method, administration, missed pills, late injections, or change in health conditions which…
options: Partner can feel IUD strings during intercourse
Difficulty persuading partner to use method
Condom squeaks or makes noise during sex
Change in timing of monthly bleeding
Unexplained vaginal bleeding (suspicious for serious condition), before evaluation
Mood changes or changes in sex drive

questions.name: Client has a method in mind - check their understanding
questions.text: Check that the client's understanding of the method is accurate. Support their choice if they are medically eligible, and discuss how to use the method and what to do about side effects.
questions.detail: WHO DAK decision support FP.DT.06

questions.name: No method in mind - allow the most time
questions.text: New clients with no method in mind need the most time. Discuss the client's situation and plans, what matters most to them about a method, and which of the methods available here fit what they describe.
questions.detail: WHO DAK decision support FP.DT.06

questions.name: Screen for medical eligibility
questions.detail: FP.B11.4. Screen for medical eligibility

questions.name: Current medications
questions.detail: Medications the client is currently taking
options: NRTIs (e.g. ABC, TDF, AZT, 3TC, DDI, FTC, C265, D4T)
Protease inhibitors (e.g. ATV/r, LPV/r, DRV/r, RTV)
Anticonvulsant therapy (e.g. phenytoin, carbamazepine, barbiturates, primidone, topiramate, oxcarbazepine)
Antimicrobial therapy with rifampicin or rifabutin

questions.name: Health condition(s)
questions.detail: Health conditions that are relevant to determining medical eligibility for contraceptive methods
options: Severe trauma to the genital tract
History of hypertension, but blood pressure cannot be evaluated
History of hypertension during pregnancy, and blood pressure can be evaluated
Adequately controlled hypertension, and blood pressure can be evaluated
Multiple risk factors for arterial cardiovascular disease
SLE with positive (or unknown) antiphospholipid antibodies
DVT/PE and established on anticoagulant therapy
Heavy or prolonged vaginal bleeding patterns
Gestational trophoblastic disease with decreasing or undetectable ß-hCG level
Gestational trophoblastic disease with persistently elevated β-hCG levels or malignant disease
Anatomical abnormalities that distort the uterine cavity
Anatomical abnormalities that do not distort the uterine cavity
Past pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) with subsequent pregnancy
Past pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) without subsequent pregnancy
Symptomatic gall bladder disease (treated by cholecystectomy)
Current symptoms of gall bladder disease
Benign focal nodular hyperplasia of the liver
Severe trauma to the gental tract
Fixed uterus due to previous surgery or infection
Chronic disease that elevates body temperature
Acute disease that elevates body temperature
